description: Operating limits of the DC Conventional points (PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §5). HAND-WRITTEN and reviewed. tools/build-conv-parameter-registry.mjs merges these rows into data/conv-parameters.json as `limits`; js/conv/point-status.js reads them from there. A page never types a limit (P-1). Bounds may be null; where set they must satisfy lo_alarm <= lo_warn < hi_warn <= hi_alarm. `nominal` is the value the point sits at in the NORMAL scenario (engine value or the page's simulated base) and is what the P-6 history check replays. `migratedFrom` names the page literal a row replaces.

rows.label: TCS supply temperature (CDU TT-01)
rows.basis: Owner decision OD-3 (PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §12): warn 37 / alarm 40 °C high, warn 18 / alarm 15 °C low until a site design is given. Supersedes the page band 17–45 °C.

rows.label: TCS specific flow (CDU FT-01)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi] (the page's bandState rule).

rows.label: TCS ΔT (CDU ΔT-01)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi].

rows.label: TCS loop differential pressure (CDU PDT-02)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi].

rows.label: TCS system pressure (CDU PT-01)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi].

rows.label: TCS reservoir level (CDU LT-01)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi].

rows.label: CDU heat-exchanger approach (TT-Δ)
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed: warn outside [lo, hi], alarm outside [0.9·lo, 1.1·hi].

rows.label: White-space average air temperature
rows.basis: ASHRAE 2015 Thermal Guidelines: recommended 18–27 °C (all classes) = normal band; Class A1 allowable 15–32 °C = alarm bounds. Same values the page typed.

source.ref: ASHRAE TC 9.9, Data Center Power Equipment Thermal Guidelines and Best Practices (2016), Table 2 'ASHRAE 2015 Thermal Guidelines' (read 2026-11-20)
source.section: Table 2: Recommended A1–A4 18 to 27 °C; Allowable A1 15 to 32 °C

rows.migratedFrom: dc-conventional.html:1540 if (t > 32) crit; else if (t > 27 || t < 18) warn

rows.label: White-space average relative humidity
rows.basis: Page band migrated as typed (warn outside 20–80 % RH). The 2015 ASHRAE envelope is dew-point based (A1 allowable 8–80 % RH, recommended to 60 % RH); the page's RH-only band is kept until a dew-point point exists.

rows.label: Rack inlet air temperature
rows.basis: High side as typed on the data hall (doc-03 alarm rules: warn > 27 °C, crit > 30 °C; 27 °C = ASHRAE recommended maximum). Low side = ASHRAE recommended 18 °C / A1 allowable 15 °C.

source.ref: ASHRAE TC 9.9 (2016) Table 2 'ASHRAE 2015 Thermal Guidelines' (read 2026-11-20); datahall.html doc-03 alarm rules
source.section: Recommended 18 to 27 °C; A1 allowable 15 to 32 °C; doc-03 crit 30 °C

rows.label: Rack load (share of rack rating)
rows.basis: Page rule migrated as typed (doc-03 alarm rules: warn rack > 85 % rating, crit > 95 %).

rows.label: CRAH supply air temperature
rows.basis: Supply air is the rack inlet plane in this model: ASHRAE 2015 recommended 18–27 °C = normal band, Class A1 allowable 15–32 °C = alarm bounds.

source.ref: ASHRAE TC 9.9, Data Center Power Equipment Thermal Guidelines and Best Practices (2016), Table 2 'ASHRAE 2015 Thermal Guidelines' (read 2026-11-20)
source.section: Table 2: Recommended 18 to 27 °C; Allowable A1 15 to 32 °C

rows.label: Chilled-water supply temperature
rows.basis: Engine design value 19.4 °C ± a declared margin: warn ±1.5 K, alarm ±3.0 K.

source.ref: js/conv-engine.js cooling.chws_c; margin declared in PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §5 basis order 2

rows.label: Chilled-water return temperature
rows.basis: Engine design value 27 °C + a declared margin: warn +0.8 K, alarm +1.5 K (the margins chiller-plant.html typed as LOOP_T2_WARNING_MAX / LOOP_T2_ALARM_MAX). High side only: a cold return is not an operating limit of the plant.

source.ref: js/conv-engine.js cooling.chwr_c; margins migrated from chiller-plant.html (PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §5 basis order 2)

rows.label: Condenser-water supply temperature
rows.basis: Engine design value 32 °C ± a declared margin: warn ±1.5 K, alarm ±3.0 K.

source.ref: js/conv-engine.js cooling.cdw_supply_c; margin declared in PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §5 basis order 2

rows.label: UPS system load (2N, one side)
rows.basis: 2N: above 50 % one side could not carry the other's load on a transfer (alarm = redundancy lost); warn 5 points before it.

rows.label: Genset load (share of unit rating)

nominal.ref: ASSUMED operating point inside the engine's max loading

rows.basis: Warn at the engine's declared maximum genset loading (electrical.genset_max_loading = 0.8); alarm at the unit rating (100 %).

rows.label: Bulk fuel tank level (UST-01)
rows.basis: The engine's own level setpoints: fuel.level_low_pct 60 (LO), fuel.level_low_low_pct 30 (LO-LO), fuel.level_overfill_pct 95 (overfill).
rows.migratedFrom: fuel-system.html:1183-1184 ustPct < 30 crit / < 60 warn; fuel-system.html:1191 ustPct > 95 warn

rows.label: Day-tank level (running genset)

nominal.ref: midpoint of the fill cycle: fill start 50 … fill stop 90 (control registry conv.fuel-system.day_tank_fill_start / _stop)

rows.basis: The fuel page's day-tank control numbers (control registry, PRD-SETPOINT-SIM P9): fill opens on a running set below 50 % and closes at 90 %, so while fill is available a running set's tank never falls below 45 % (1.8 h at rated burn): below 45 % means the fill has failed (warn); low-low 25 % (alarm). Corrected 2026-11-26: the band said warn 30 % from an older page (DT_LOW 30) while the page had moved to 50 / 45; law C16 keeps them equal.

rows.label: Fire main pressure
rows.basis: Low side from the fire mimic: duty fire pump FP-1 starts at 10.5 bar (warn below it: the main is no longer held by the jockey 11.5/12.8 bar), low-pressure alarm at 8.5 bar. High side ASSUMED (PN16 pipework: warn 14, alarm 16 bar). NFPA 20 clauses not read: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Fuel autonomy (usable fuel / consumption)
rows.basis: Alarm below the 24 h backup-power SLA that fuel-system.html declares (SLA_HR); dc-conventional.html typed warn < 24 h / crit < 12 h in its alarm strip, the SLA reading is kept because it is the contract (merge 2026-11-21): N+1 autonomy must exceed it. No separate warning band is declared: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Autonomy margin over the 24 h SLA
rows.basis: Autonomy minus the 24 h SLA; the page reported FAIL when it was below zero (slaMarginHr) and PASS at or above. Same rule, now from the registry.

rows.label: Raw water tank level (TK-101)
rows.basis: Alarm below 30 %, warning below 40 %: the page's own raw-tank thresholds, migrated as typed. A local alarm-philosophy choice, no standard clause read: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Domestic / treated tank level (TK-402)
rows.basis: Alarm below 40 %, warning below 50 %: the page's own domestic-tank thresholds, migrated as typed. ASSUMED.

rows.label: Media filter differential pressure (FLT-201)
rows.basis: Warning above 0.65 bar, alarm (backwash) above 0.80 bar: the page's filter thresholds, migrated as typed. A local backwash philosophy: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Treated water TDS
rows.basis: Warning above 350 ppm, alarm above 500 ppm (the page's treated-water reject limit), migrated as typed. ASSUMED: no standard clause read.

rows.label: UV lamp intensity (UV-401)
rows.basis: Alarm below 70 %, warning below 85 % of nominal lamp intensity: the page's UV thresholds, migrated as typed. ASSUMED.

rows.label: Instant WUE (site)
rows.basis: Warning above the engine's WUE design target (water.wue_target_l_per_kwh = 1.3 L/kWh), the page's own rule wueComputed > WUE_TARGET. No alarm band is declared: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Fire-water reserve tank level
rows.basis: Warning at or below 80 % (the page's TANK_LOW_PCT, where make-up supply engages), alarm at or below 60 % (TANK_LL_PCT low-low): migrated as typed. A local alarm philosophy, no NFPA 22 clause read: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Network link / core utilisation

nominal.ref: ict.html TRAFFIC_SCENARIO 14.2 Gbps / NETWORK_CAPACITY_BASIS core usable 40 Gbps

rows.basis: The utilisation bands ict.html already applied (utilClass and the status-bar Core Util: warn above 60 %, bad above 80 %), moved here. A page-authored operating policy, not a published standard.
rows.migratedFrom: ict.html utilClass(p): p > 80 bad, p > 60 warn; renderBottomBar CORE_UTIL > 80 / > 60

rows.label: BMS poll freshness (age of the last telemetry)
rows.basis: The stale-telemetry rule the page states (warn if stale telemetry > 60 s), moved here. No alarm bound: the page declares none.

source.ref: ict.html Poll Freshness note and the Stale rule line (PRD-CONV-POINT-STATUS-TREND §5 basis order 3)

rows.migratedFrom: ict.html caps note 'warn if stale telemetry >60s'

rows.label: Transformer loading (share of nameplate MVA / kVA)
rows.basis: Duplicated transformers (TX-1 / TX-2, the distribution pair of a stream): each must stay at or below 50 % for the other to carry the whole load, so above 50 % redundancy is already used (warn); alarm at the nameplate rating (100 %). The engine's N-1 loading (hv_tx_load_pct_n1 72.7 %, dist_tx_load_pct_contingency 96.9 % at design load) is what an operator switching in the simulation reaches. No clause read: ASSUMED.

rows.label: Hall cooling margin (headroom over demand)

nominal.ref: ASSUMED design target: no engine parameter publishes a cooling-margin target

rows.basis: The page rule migrated as typed: datahall.html coloured the Cooling Margin warning below 5 %. Low side only. The alarm bound 0 % (demand equal to the available capacity) and the nominal 10 % are ASSUMED. The engine's present margin is 0.53 % (headroom 40 kW on 7,500 kW), so the point reads Warning today, as the page already coloured it.
